claims.text: Iteratively adapting training sample weights with a theoretically grounded model addresses different types of algorithmic bias.
Data repairing approaches that weight training samples of sensitive groups based on misclassification error exhibit limited success in mitigating bias.

evidence.description: The authors present a process that iteratively adapts training sample weights to achieve trade-offs between accuracy and fairness objectives like disparate impact or disparate mistreatment elimination.
Previous attempts to repair training data by weighting sensitive group samples based on misclassification error lead to shortcomings and limited success.

methodologies.name: Adaptive Sensitive Reweighting
methodologies.description: An iterative process that adapts training sample weights using a theoretically grounded model to optimize trade-offs between accuracy and fairness objectives.

limitations.text: Previous data repairing approaches suffer from shortcomings when weighting training samples of sensitive groups based on misclassification error.
